clue.text: Aimless mass follows organised party

indicators.note: follows places the mass letter after the pieces built from organised party

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it, so organised gives RAN
a do is an informal word for a party
M is the standard abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A political party so badly organised that a crowd drifts after it without purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random has no plan or aim behind it, so it is aimless.

clue.text: Improper young lady supporting adult

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means sitting beneath, so the young lady comes under the adult letter

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
a miss is a girl or young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl helping a grown-up in some improper way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is wrong or out of place, so improper.

clue.text: Some command is sent eradicating rebel

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An order is issued to wipe out the insurgent.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter refuses to accept official views, so is a rebel against authority.

clue.text: Chap's going round English capital

indicators.note: going round says the chap word surrounds the English letter

parts.note: a chap is a man, so chap's gives man's

explanation.surface: A man touring the capital city of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like London, but it means money.
explanation.definitionFit: Means are financial resources, as in a person of means, so capital.

clue.text: School is what aids in cultivation?

definitions.meaning: A famous English public school in north-west London, attended by Winston Churchill
a farm implement dragged over ploughed land to break up the soil

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which school helps things grow, as if education were gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a well-known English boarding school and a spiked frame used by farmers to prepare soil for crops.

clue.text: Hard sweetheart, plain and cold

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, E
artless means simple and unaffected, plain

explanation.surface: A tough, plain-speaking lover with no warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is read as the heart (middle letter) of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heartless lacks feeling or pity, which is to be cold.

clue.text: One moves chopper up and down?

definitions.text: One moves chopper up and down?

indicators.note: in a down answer, up and down says it reads the same either way

parts.note: the spinning blade that drives a helicopter, slang chopper

explanation.surface: A riddle about what lifts and lowers a helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and 'up and down' also says the word reads the same both ways in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter's spinning blades raise and lower the aircraft, so they move it vertically.

clue.text: Daunting cricket deliveries by a side

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
a wing is a side, as of a building or army

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler's spell against one team is intimidating.
explanation.definitionFit: Overawing means filling someone with awe so they are subdued, which is daunting them.

clue.text: Confusion of curious cat losing tail

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or curious

indicators.note: losing tail says the cat word drops its last letter

parts.note: puss is a familiar name for a cat

explanation.surface: A puzzled, nosy cat that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy disturbance, a commotion or confusion.

clue.text: Smell from head of sea fish

indicators.note: head of picks the opening letter of sea

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A smell rising from the head of a sea fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong foul odour, a bad smell.

clue.text: Dimwit embraced by American constituents

indicators.note: embraced by says the fool word is held inside the American abbreviation

parts.note: a nit (nitwit) is a fool, a dimwit

explanation.surface: A foolish politician welcomed warmly by the American voters he represents.
explanation.definitionFit: Units are the component parts of a whole, which is what constituents are.

clue.text: Likely employing craft workers for flat

indicators.note: employing means using or taking in, so the likely word holds the other pieces

parts.note: apt means likely, as in apt to happen
art is a synonym of craft or skill
men is a common crossword word for workers or staff

explanation.surface: A building firm likely to hire craftsmen to fit out a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employing' is read as taking on or holding, so 'Likely' wraps the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a flat is a self-contained dwelling on one floor, the American apartment.

clue.text: Crew by ship's hold

parts.note: a posse is a gang or crew of people
SS (steamship) is the prefix for a ship's name

explanation.surface: Sailors standing beside their ship's cargo hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' looks like the ship's cargo space, but it is a verb meaning to own.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to own it or keep it, which is to hold it.

clue.text: Discontented referee back in exercise ground

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters within the exercise word

parts.note: to train is to exercise or work out

indicators.note: back says those kept letters are read in reverse order
with its contents taken away, only the outer letters of referee stay

explanation.surface: An unhappy referee goes back into training on the practice ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discontented' means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters of the official.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features, so it is ground.

clue.text: Show act peels, dancing around clubs

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap the clubs letter
dancing letters move about, so act peels is rearranged

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, a suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A stage act where performers strip off layers while dancing around nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' turns ACT PEELS into SPETACLE (one arrangement), and 'around' wraps it round C after SPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is an impressive public display or performance, a show.

clue.text: For example, worker in train plant

parts.note: EG (exempli gratia) means for example

indicators.note: in places the worker inside the train word

parts.note: a line is a train or queue of people or things
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A worker on a train, perhaps planting something.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweetbriar, a wild rose, so a plant.

clue.text: Miss head after class's first friendship

indicators.note: after places the miss and head words after that letter
first picks the opening letter of the word class

parts.note: to lose a chance is to miss it
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A young lady at the head of the class making friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young lady but is the verb; 'head' is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeness is intimacy between people, so friendship.

clue.text: Singular desire to get whip

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: Someone with an odd longing to own a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: A swish is a cane or switch, a thin whip that hisses through the air.

clue.text: Post chain's not loose

indicators.note: loose letters are free to move, so chain's not is rearranged

explanation.surface: A post with its chain not tied fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright bar or support, a post.

clue.text: Regret consumes large Republican leader

indicators.note: consumes means swallows, so the regret word takes the large letter inside it

parts.note: to rue something is to regret it
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Remorse eats away at a big Republican party boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler governs a country, so is its leader.

clue.text: Sunnier seeing leather finally on willow

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above, so that letter sits on the willow word
finally picks the closing letter of leather

parts.note: an osier is a willow used in basket-making

explanation.surface: Brighter days as leather strikes willow, the cricket ball meeting the bat.
explanation.walkthrough: Leather and willow are the materials of a cricket ball and bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosier means more hopeful or optimistic, so sunnier in outlook.

clue.text: In convulsions, laugh, turning offensive

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, across their joins

explanation.surface: Someone convulsed with laughter whose fit of giggles becomes rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective meaning rude, but here it is a noun, a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce attack, and an offensive is a military assault.

clue.text: Cards Jack's holding out occasionally

indicators.note: holding says the sailor word wraps the picked letters

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, so jack gives tar

indicators.note: occasionally picks every other letter of out

explanation.surface: A card player holding the jack, sometimes playing it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarots are a pack of picture cards used in fortune-telling.

clue.text: Devout following return of Queen

parts.note: since means after or following, as in since the war

indicators.note: return of says the royal letters are turned to run backwards

parts.note: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the royal cipher for the Queen

explanation.surface: A pious courtier who has followed the Queen since her homecoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Devout can mean earnest and heartfelt, as in a devout wish, which is sincere.

clue.text: Escape, largely using deceptive evasion, initially

definitions.text: Escape, largely using deceptive evasion, initially

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each word before it

explanation.surface: Escape, mostly by tricky dodging.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of eluding.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude is to get away from someone, typically by cunning dodging.

clue.text: Support victim being picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as by a radio, so the victim word is said aloud

parts.note: a sucker is a gullible person, the victim of a con

explanation.surface: Help for a person who was just lifted up or arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is help given in time of need, which is support.

clue.text: Beaches in both ends of Seychelles?

indicators.note: in places the joining word between the two end letters
ends of picks the first and last letters of Seychelles, an S and an S

parts.note: both pairs with and, as in both this and that, so it stands for the joining word

explanation.surface: Wondering whether both tips of the Seychelles islands are sandy beaches.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a description, both ends of Seychelles are 'S and S'; the parse puts AND (from 'both') 'in' between the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sands are stretches of sandy shore, so beaches.

clue.text: Sitting on lake is river bird

indicators.note: in a down answer, sitting on means placed above, so the river sits over the lake letter

parts.note: the Ouse is the name of several English rivers
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A river bird perched on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river bird' looks like the definition; 'river' is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An ousel is an old name for the blackbird or the dipper, a bird.

clue.text: A nice pure spread for gourmet

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters of A nice pure are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tasty, wholesome spread on toast that would please a food connoisseur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like something for toast, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is a person devoted to fine food and drink, a gourmet.

clue.text: Training for teachers or pupils here?

definitions.meaning: ... (In-Service Education and Training) days are British school days set aside for staff training
pupils grouped by ability are placed in a set

explanation.surface: A question about whether a school day is for staff training or for teaching children.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym names staff training days, and split as two words it says where streamed schoolchildren are placed.

clue.text: Depression gets you break from work

definitions.meaning: a hollow or alcove set back in a wall or surface
a pause in work, as when parliament or a court rises

explanation.surface: Feeling low earns you a pause from your job.
explanation.definitionFit: Recess names both an indentation in a surface and a period when work or business is suspended.

clue.text: Individual small fireplace

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
an ingle is a fireplace or hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: A personal little fireplace for one room.
explanation.definitionFit: Single means one alone, separate, which is individual.
